isd.text: Thraben, the High City of Innistrad, is where the church conceals its greatest secret: Avacyn vanished from the Cathedral of Avacyn there, and the church has kept the truth of her disappearance from Innistrad's people. With the army recalled to Thraben's walls, outlying villages were left to fend for themselves while werewolf attacks and hauntings increased.
Behind it lay an old battle on the Helvault, where the demon Griselbrand challenged Avacyn and she drove him into the silver mass, only to be drawn in herself by the backlash of her binding spell.

Then Geralf and Gisa Cecani unleashed ghouls, skaabs and Grimgrin on Thraben's walls in the Siege of Thraben. Geralf sneaked into the city to murder the Lunarch Mikaeus while Gisa's dead battered the gates until the main wall fell, and Lothar, tormented by demonic voices, threw himself off the ramparts.

Thalia, who became Guardian of Thraben in his place, burned the outer ring with stolen thatch, incinerating the undead and halting the siege. Mikaeus was secretly entombed beneath the Cathedral, where Liliana later exhumed his corpse and learned that Griselbrand was imprisoned in the Helvault.

dka.text: In Dark Ascension, Thraben stands without its protector, since Griselbrand turned the Helvault against Avacyn, trapped her inside and left Innistrad with no guardian, and the Church concealed her fate by making the few priests who had witnessed it swear to secrecy.

In her absence Gisa and Geralf besiege the city, and Geralf kills Lunarch Mikaeus, whom Liliana raises as a zombie. Thalia, appointed supreme commander, rallies the defenders and declares she will not see Thraben fall to the unhallowed horde.

Gisa's army breaks the outer wall but is pushed back by fire, and Odric captures Gisa. Liliana then forces Thalia to destroy the Helvault by threatening her soldiers, which unleashes Avacyn and the demons.
Even the cathedral is not safe, as devils infiltrate its lower levels, cracking pillars and burning archives.

avr.text: Avacyn Restored tells how Thraben came to guard the Helvault without knowing what it held. Mikaeus decided to keep the shard's nature secret, telling Lothar only to protect it, and Thalia, who had earned a place among Lothar's elite guardians by rescuing an old man from a howlpack, later took the same oath.

When Geralf and Gisa besieged Thraben with their ghoulish army, Thalia outwitted them by trapping the undead with straw and burning them in a great circle of fire. Lothar plunged from a high wall, and Mikaeus, killed in the assault, was entombed in secret beneath the cathedral.

Thalia became the Guardian of Thraben, unknowingly keeping Avacyn sealed, until Liliana raised Mikaeus's corpse, learned Griselbrand was trapped in the Helvault, and forced Thalia to destroy it during the siege, releasing the demons and Avacyn.

soi.text: Thraben is where Shadows over Innistrad draws its threads together. Jace announces that he must go to Thraben to find Avacyn, while Liliana warns that Avacyn will kill him. Within the city, Thalia has lost faith, confiding her fear that Avacyn's time in the Helvault corrupted her and declaring that she can no longer serve Avacyn and her church.

She storms into the Lunarch Council and accuses Bishop Jerren of communion with Ormendahl and of leading the Skirsdag, but the council calls for her execution. Odric, shaken by the council's cruelty, goes to her cell and fights alongside Grete to free her, and the three leave Thraben on horseback.

In the cathedral, Tamiyo finds Jace mad and steadies him, and the two link minds. When Avacyn arrives with her wings stained with blood, Tamiyo fights her with the story Winter's Howl but Avacyn breaks free and tortures Jace.

Sorin crashes through the skylight and reveals that he is her creator, and Avacyn, seeing the fires she set and the innocents she slew, condemns him as the greatest evil of the world. After a savage fight that ends in the cellar where she was made, Sorin destroys her by performing his ritual in reverse, leaving the cathedral feeling vacant.

emn.text: In Eldritch Moon Thraben becomes the battlefield on which Innistrad's fate is decided. Avacyn, corrupted by Emrakul's presence, attacks humanity and is destroyed by her creator Sorin Markov in the cathedral, and Sorin, trapped in stone, watches Emrakul drift across Gavony toward the city.

Thalia calls on Saint Traft to summon the spirits of the dead, who possess and shield her soldiers, and her army passes through the Outer Wall and fights alongside vampires through the streets. Before the cathedral looms a huge fused angel of flesh, tentacles and wings, and Thalia is slashed down when she attacks it on her gryff.

Sigarda arrives and disowns her fused sisters, and with Saint Traft's help Thalia lifts Avacyn's spear, is given glowing angelic wings, and drives it through the creature's back. Sigarda bursts from the dying angel-thing's chest, though a tidal wave of corrupted monsters soon smashes into the plaza.

Elsewhere in the city, the Gatewatch is trapped in a market square after Chandra's firestorm, and Nissa's attempt to begin a planar glyph fails when a darker vine strangles her. Liliana's zombie army forms a perimeter around them, and she appears with the Chain Veil and wipes out the mutated creatures, rescuing the Gatewatch.

mid.text: Thraben in Midnight Hunt is a ruin. After Emrakul was sealed in Innistrad's moon, the city lay in ruins, and two years later Gisa took control of Liliana's abandoned zombie army and made Thraben her own, easily defeating her suitor Wilhelt's army and forcing him to leave.
Thalia, Odric and the cathars refuse to abandon the city and keep waging war on the zombies, so cathars still patrol its ruins.

Here Katilda sends Arlinn and the Gatewatch to begin their search for the Moonsilver Key. The group finds Thraben destroyed and full of zombies, and Kaya scouts alone and finds an old book showing the Key was given to an ancestor of the Betzold family.
Among the zombie army they find Bishop Worrin Betzold, now a zombie, and get the name Dennick from him before Arlinn kills him out of mercy.
